### Historical audit: S0092, visible chunk 1 of 3

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/replay_s1/H_start/H_start/replay_development/commons_2238909/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to its JSONL lines. Neither the referenced images nor the other chunks are visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Goal — line 1 | The student was asked to reconstruct a single indoor photograph as an editable, multi-mesh SceneAct/Blender scene, matching viewpoint, placement, materials and occlusion. The student’s own anchor comments interpret it as an archive corridor; that interpretation is not independent image verification (line 3). |
| First build — student response line 3; execute line 4 | Code constructs multiple objects: architecture, 25 shelving banks, a book bay, carts and ceiling fixtures. Banks group separately modeled panels, wheels and cranks; their actual physical connections are not geometrically verified. Colors and roughness are specified, but no surface texture is demonstrated. No articulated human pose is apparent in the code. Camera and lights are explicitly configured. |
| Validation — execution result line 5 | Step 1 reports `ok: true`, a saved render and blend file. The render log reports 16 samples despite the program setting 32; the record does not establish why. This is execution success, not visual or geometric correctness. Lines 6–7 select step 1. |
| Autonomous correction — student request line 8, response line 10, execute line 11 | The student received the step-1 result and render for comparison. Its own comments diagnose a displaced vanishing point, washed-out floor/cabinets and a broad foreground cabinet side. It then moved and turned the camera, darkened materials, changed lighting and emission handling, and added label/sign details. These diagnoses and intended effects are student claims, not independently verified image findings. |
| Second validation — execution result line 12; selects lines 13–14 | Step 2 also reports `ok: true` and a saved image and blend file; it is selected in the visible events. The visible excerpt ends there, so final submission and later review remain unknown. |

**Teacher input and adoption:** No teacher message, detection, diagnosis or proposed update is visible in this chunk. The comparison instruction and render in line 8 are harness feedback, not evidence of teacher input. The subsequent revision demonstrates response to that feedback, not adoption of unseen teacher advice.

**Assessment and uncertainty:** Two nonempty programs executed successfully; overall reconstruction correctness is **unknown**, not formal success or demonstrated algorithm failure. The available record does not independently establish object visibility, material appearance, part contact, pose accuracy, camera alignment or lighting quality. The student’s camera and brightness hypotheses were tested by a second execution, but its visual outcome is unavailable here.

**Lessons:** Transferably, a successful render should be separated from visual validation, and global camera hypotheses from local object adjustments. Task-specific choices—archive shelving, book placement and the proposed vanishing point—remain unverified interpretations of the inaccessible reference.
